scope.description: Dedicated Canadian organization research for Ultra Maritime, centred on its Dartmouth operation, documented undersea-warfare technologies, Sea Tracker collaboration, and Royal Canadian Navy work. Public evidence is kept separate from operator-provided PA-4 context.

source.title: Ultra Maritime Canada
source.locator: Proudly Atlantic Canadian, ACOA's Partnership, and Royal Canadian Navy contract sections
source.summary: The Government of Canada identifies Ultra Maritime's Dartmouth operation as a Canadian towed-array centre of excellence that develops or integrates sonobuoys, hull-mounted sonar, and towed acoustic arrays and supports Royal Canadian Navy programs.

leads.evidenceLocator: Official Government of Canada profile, Ultra Maritime product and contract pages, COVE project announcement, company contact page, and Royal Canadian Navy system factsheet
followUpQuestions: Can a durable public source explicitly connect the PA-4 identifier or Protecteur-class program context to Sea Tracker?
Which Ultra Maritime product images and logo assets are approved for the public dossier?
Which Canadian workforce figure should remain visible after the dated 2025 ACOA profile becomes stale?
leads.candidateCapabilityName: Sea Tracker Containerized Anti-Submarine Warfare System
leads.roleSpecificEvidence: Official Canadian and company sources establish a long-running Dartmouth undersea-warfare operation that develops and builds towed arrays in Canada, manufactures or integrates sonobuoys and hull-mounted sonar, supplies Royal Canadian Navy surface-combatant systems, supports River-class readiness, and is providing the modular Sea Tracker system to DRDC for experimentation with COVE and ACOA support. The reviewed sources do not use the PA-4 identifier, so that operator-provided context remains an unpublished follow-up rather than a public claim.
